title: OpenAI alert relayed through the FBI leads Espírito Santo police to detain a father a day before his stated date to kill his son
summary: OpenAI's safety systems flagged a ChatGPT user's plan to kill his 8-year-old son; alerted through the FBI, Brazilian police held him a day before his stated date.
account: In 2026 a 36-year-old farmer in São Gabriel da Palha, Espírito Santo, Brazil, told ChatGPT about a plan to kill his 8-year-old son. He said that he had offered R$50,000 to a hitman and that he had set 20 June as the date. OpenAI's safety systems flagged the account, and the company referred it to the FBI. The FBI passed it to the Ministry of Justice's CyberLab. The Polícia Civil do Espírito Santo received it on 16 June and arrested him under warrants on 19 June. Officers seized his phone, four bottles of an unidentified substance and a knotted rope. He admitted the searches but denied intent. He was freed on habeas corpus on 13 August 2026 after 54 days, under an ankle monitor and a no-contact order. The inquiry continues. BBC News Brasil reported on 14 August 2026 that the court freed him because the inquiry had run too long without a charge. Legal experts whom BBC News Brasil interviewed said that the messages justified pretrial detention. They said that the messages alone would not support a charge. The lead investigator told BBC News Brasil that OpenAI sent the user's prompts without ChatGPT's replies. In early October 2026 OpenAI closed the account of a user who said that he wanted to shoot President Lula after seeing him at a campaign event, and the company passed the data to the Federal Police.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose conversational assistant. OpenAI's moderation layer is built to route conversations that indicate plans to harm others to human reviewers. Those reviewers may refer an imminent threat to law enforcement, under a policy published 26 August 2025. The referral that triggered the arrest came from that layer working as it was built to work.
system: ChatGPT with OpenAI's safety-monitoring pipeline (automated classifiers plus human review and law-enforcement referral)

ratings.reason: The 8-year-old, and his mother who was placed under a no-contact order, were shielded from a plan that the father had dated to 20 June. Police say that the platform's information was corroborated when they arrived. He denies intent and no charge has been filed, so a life-saving effect is not established.

The Polícia Civil do Espírito Santo obtained a lead through the FBI and the Ministry of Justice CyberLab. It says that it had no other way to get it. Its cybercrime chief called the alert another path for police work. The Ministry rated it the gravest of three such alerts in Brazil.

ai_role.statement: OpenAI's automated classifiers and human reviewers flagged the user's messages, and the company chose to refer the account to the FBI. The system did not predict a crime or act on its own. The warrants, the arrest and the evidence-gathering were police and court actions. OpenAI sent only the user's prompts, not ChatGPT's replies. What the assistant said to the user, and whether it helped or hindered him, is unknown.

display.answer: The police release and the Brazilian news reports of 25 to 27 June 2026 describe the same chain from OpenAI to the FBI, the Ministry of Justice's CyberLab and the state police, and g1 cites the deputy police chief. BBC News Brasil adds the court's release, the views of legal experts and the lead investigator's account of what OpenAI sent. OpenAI's policy page of 26 August 2025 describes the referral process and does not mention this case.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: OpenAI's safety systems flagged a ChatGPT user's plan to kill his 8-year-old son; alerted through the FBI, Brazilian police held him a day before his stated date.
fields.account: In 2026 a 36-year-old farmer in São Gabriel da Palha, Espírito Santo, Brazil, told ChatGPT about a plan to kill his 8-year-old son. He said that he had offered R$50,000 to a hitman and that he had set 20 June as the date. OpenAI's safety systems flagged the account, and the company referred it to the FBI. The FBI passed it to the Ministry of Justice's CyberLab. The Polícia Civil do Espírito Santo received it on 16 June and arrested him under warrants on 19 June. Officers seized his phone, four bottles of an unidentified substance and a knotted rope. He admitted the searches but denied intent. He was freed on habeas corpus on 13 August 2026 after 54 days, under an ankle monitor and a no-contact order. The inquiry continues. BBC News Brasil reported on 14 August 2026 that the court freed him because the inquiry had run too long without a charge. Legal experts whom BBC News Brasil interviewed said that the messages justified pretrial detention. They said that the messages alone would not support a charge. The lead investigator told BBC News Brasil that OpenAI sent the user's prompts without ChatGPT's replies. In early October 2026 OpenAI closed the account of a user who said that he wanted to shoot President Lula after seeing him at a campaign event, and the company passed the data to the Federal Police.
